main_logic: Convective wind is measured as gust ratio V₃ₛ,hub / Ve50 (IEC class).
Engineering-fit logistic curves on hub gust over the IEC 50-year gust, built from IEC design speeds, the NIST fragility method and EF4 case evidence; tornado is a curve shift.

steps.name: What it covers
steps.meaning: The parts that have a curve, their share of the value, and what has none yet
steps.fact: 5 parts with a curve · 1 without one yet
paragraphs: Convective wind on wind farms: engineering-fit logistic curves on hub gust over the IEC 50-year gust, built from IEC design speeds, the NIST fragility method and EF4 case evidence; tornado is a curve shift. It names 5 parts: Blade, Tower, Nacelle, Foundation and Power electronics. Outside its scope: tropical-cyclone and hurricane wind (separate neighbouring cell). Kinds of damage it does not include: operating, feathered and yaw state are flags only, with no numeric effect.

For this hazard the wind farm is split into 5 parts: Blade, Tower, Nacelle, Foundation and Power electronics. Parts of the plant's value with no curve yet: SCADA and controls, electrical collection, substation and civil infrastructure (reviewed secondary units, no curve).

The damage ratio is a share of each part's default share of the physical replaceable base (blade 0.173, tower 0.169, nacelle 0.345, foundation 0.062, power electronics 0.037), times the exposed turbine fraction. The files state no plant-level dollar figure for this asset. Shares of the plant's physical value, as the cell states them: Blade 17 %, Tower 17 %, Nacelle 34 %, Foundation 6 % and Power electronics 4 %.

steps.name: How damage is worked out
steps.meaning: How the hazard is measured, the shape of the curve, and the site adjustments
steps.fact: gust ratio V₃ₛ,hub / Ve50 → an S-curve
paragraphs: Damage is read against gust ratio V₃ₛ,hub / Ve50 (IEC class). The curve is an S-shaped curve: little damage, then a steep rise, then a plateau (logistic). The input, in the catalogue's words: hub-height 3-second gust (m/s), or 10 m gust with a height bridge, divided by the IEC class 50-year gust (Ve50 = 1.4 x Vref); tornado via an EF-scale gust proxy; no fixed range (extrapolation warns).

The adjustments — which selectors and conditioners change the curve — are written in the dossier; no seven-step audit table exists as a file. A site-condition adapter has not been written for this cell.

Of the 22 parameters, 1 is published, 5 are borrowed and 16 are our judgment.
